approach: Add `athena_core::triage`. `Athena::triage(items, caps, ui)` loads the records and returns early if the run is nested or nothing is open. It then makes one steward-role model call (verifier model and budget, as `steward::consult` does). The call carries the focus, the open items (title, rung, effective priority and setter, age, dependencies) and the failure classes of the last two days. The answer is JSON: `changes` (item, priority, reason) and `close` (item, reason). A pure function `plan_changes` validates the answer. It drops unknown or non-open items, bad levels, empty reasons, no-op changes, and any item whose latest priority record has no author, because a person set it. It applies the caps by counting every open item already urgent or high, person-set ones included, and updates the count after each applied change. `PriorityRecord` gains optional `set_by` and `reason`, which are absent for person records. Applied changes are committed as steward-authored priority records. Each `close` entry becomes a steward `WorkItem` of kind Proposal on the brief-requirements rung, which is above the steward's limit, so only a proposal is recorded. The code writes no outcome or close record. `Steps` gets a defaulted `triage() -> Vec<String>` method, like `review_passes`. `drain_with` prints its lines right after the review passes (the Hestia sweep) and before the queue is read. `RealSteps::triage` builds the items from its own `queue()` plan entries. A failed call returns one `triage failed: …; the drain goes on` line and the drain continues. `RealSteps::person_set` stops counting steward-authored records as a person's word.

decisions.choice: Add optional `set_by` and `reason` fields to the existing `athena.priority/1` record (serde default, skipped when None). A record with no author counts as a person's.
decisions.reason: The brief says priority records are attributed to the steward and carry a reason, and that no new record kind is added. Old records still parse. `validate` requires a reason when `set_by` is set and none when it is not, so a steward record without a reason is refused.

rejected.why: The brief says no new kind. It would also need new store, plan and status handling.

rejected.option: Record the author only in a commit trailer
rejected.why: The setter could not be read back from `Records`, so the person-set rule could not be enforced from the records.

decisions.choice: The triage call is made in `athena-core` (`Athena::triage`), and the CLI passes in the plan entries it already builds in `RealSteps::queue()`.
decisions.reason: The rung, effective priority and dependencies are already computed there by `entry_of`. Reusing them avoids a second copy of that logic. The model plumbing (`agent_spec`, `invoke_and_record`, `stash_invocation`) sits beside the steward in core.

rejected.option: Recompute rung and priority inside core from `Records`

decisions.choice: Seam: a defaulted `Steps::triage(&self) -> Vec<String>` called once in `drain_with` straight after the `review_passes` loop.
decisions.reason: It follows the existing `review_passes` pattern. A failed call is one printed line, not an error, so the drain cannot stop on it. Every stub `Steps` keeps compiling, since the default is empty.

rejected.why: The drain loop is generic over `Steps` and has no `Athena`. Stubs would then trigger model calls.

decisions.choice: A close proposal is written as a `WorkItem` (kind Proposal, rung BriefRequirements, key `triage-close:<job>`, evidence the job). It is skipped if the key is already known. No applier is called and no request is queued.
decisions.reason: BriefRequirements is above the steward's `highest_rung` (DefaultsConventions) and above `Ladder::HIGHEST_SELF_CHANGE`, so by `may_change` it is proposal-only. A person decides it with `athena approve-work`. The module has no code path that writes an outcome or close record, so criterion 6 holds by construction and is also tested.

rejected.option: Let the model's priority answer include a 'closed' state
rejected.why: This is a close and is out of scope.

decisions.choice: The caps count every open item already urgent or high, then update the count as each change is applied. Changes are applied in the model's order.
decisions.reason: This matches the plan's caps, which count person-set items. It gives a deterministic result for a fixed answer. A plan-time demotion would still apply on top of this.

rejected.option: Apply everything and let `Plan::build_with` demote the extras
rejected.why: Records would be written that the caps then override, and the drain would print changes that did not hold.

decisions.choice: The deterministic fake answers a triage prompt (recognised by its `# Steward triage` heading) with an empty `changes` and `close`. Tests wrap `deterministic_turn` with a script that returns the scripted triage answer or a failed turn.
decisions.reason: A real drain through the fake must not fail on triage. `FakeTurn` already carries both outcomes. Only the model's answer is faked; the validation, caps and writing under test run for real.

rejected.option: Let triage reuse the `{items: []}` steward answer
rejected.why: The shapes differ, and a silent parse failure would hide bugs.

decisions.choice: No refusal or matching rule is added or changed, so `refusal_corpus` is not a demonstration.
decisions.reason: The answer parser ignores invalid entries. It does not parse requests, acceptance bullets or reading checks, which are what the corpus covers.

files.purpose: The triage duty. It holds the prompt brief (heading `# Steward triage`) and the answer schema and types. `Athena::triage` makes the call. The pure `plan_changes` applies validation, the person-set guard and the caps. It writes the priority records and the close-proposal work items in one records commit. `set_by_person(job)` is a helper. No close code.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix anything they report. Confirm with `git diff --stat` that no governance file changed. There is no refusal or matching rule here, so `refusal_corpus` is not part of the checks.

risks.risk: Steward-authored priority records are read as a person's word by `person_set`, so the plan never demotes them and the caps are not enforced on them.
risks.mitigation: `RealSteps::person_set` uses `triage::set_by_person`, which looks only at the latest record's author. A test checks that a steward-set urgent item over the cap is demoted by the plan.

risks.risk: Old priority records have no author. Reading a missing author as 'person' is right for them, but a malformed steward record could pass as a person's.
risks.mitigation: `validate` makes `reason` and `set_by` go together, and `deny_unknown_fields` stays. The unit tests cover both forms.

risks.risk: The model names a job id that does not exist or is not open (running, closed), or returns bad JSON or a bad level.
risks.mitigation: `plan_changes` keeps only ids from the supplied open items and only the four known levels, and needs a non-empty one-line reason. Bad JSON counts as a failed call and prints a `triage failed` line.

risks.risk: Triage runs on every drain and costs a call even when nothing is open.
risks.mitigation: No model call when no item is open, or when the run is nested. Tested through the invocation count in the script.

risks.risk: Two drains, or a person, write a priority record for the same job at the same time, so `n` collides.
risks.mitigation: `n` is computed from the records just loaded, as in `set_priority`. The commit goes through the same `commit_records` gate. A collision fails the commit, and the failure becomes a note and the drain goes on.

risks.risk: A cap skip is silent, because the brief asks for one line per change only.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated behavior. The tests assert the records and the line count. A skipped-proposal line can be added later if wanted.

risks.risk: The producer works in a snapshot with no `records/` directory, and `athena.toml` is governance and must not change.
risks.mitigation: Tests build their own fixtures. The caps come from the code default (3 and 10) through `Config::priority_caps()`, so no config edit is needed.

demonstrations.method: Integration test `triage_writes_steward_priority_records_within_caps_and_leaves_person_set_items` in `crates/athena-cli/tests/triage.rs`. It runs the real drain over real `Records`. Setup: a `Fixture`, `athena.set_focus("speed first")`, and 6 queued complete requests (path plus bullet, so nothing is read). One request gets `athena.set_priority(id, "low")`, a person's record. The `Steps` wrapper delegates `triage`, `queue`, `plan_entry`, `job_history`, `priority_caps` and `person_set` to a real `RealSteps` and stubs `run`, `land`, `rate` and `check_page`, as the `Replay` wrapper in `tests/drain.rs` does. The fake answer proposes urgent for 4 normal requests (the default cap is 3) and also urgent for the person-set one.
demonstrations.observes: After `drain::drain`, `Records::load` shows: three steward priority records at urgent, each with `set_by == Some("steward")` and the reason from the answer, each passing `check_record_file`. The fourth urgent proposal, over the cap, has no new record. The person-set request still has exactly its original record, so its latest priority is unchanged. The count of urgent items after the drain is at most 3.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the triage pass no steward priority record is written. Without the person-set guard the person's low item turns urgent. Without the cap check a fourth urgent record appears.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `athena_cli::drain::drain`, which calls `Steps::triage`, which for the real steps calls `Athena::triage`. The fake is a `Script` closure injected through `Fixture::athena(script)` that returns the scripted answer for a steward-role invocation whose prompt has the triage heading, and `deterministic_turn` otherwise. The script helper is added to `tests/common/mod.rs` in the steps. The `Steps::triage` hook and `Athena::triage` do not exist yet and are added by the plan steps. `Fixture`, `RealSteps` (public fields), `Lander` stubs and `Lines` exist today (read).

demonstrations.method: Two tests in `crates/athena-cli/tests/triage.rs`. (a) `a_failed_triage_call_prints_a_note_and_the_drain_goes_on`: the script returns a failed `FakeTurn` (non-success outcome) for the triage prompt. The drain runs with two queued requests, and the `Steps` wrapper records which jobs were run. (b) `the_drain_prints_one_line_per_applied_change`: with a good answer that changes 2 items, the lines collected by the drain's `Lines` `Ui` are counted.
demonstrations.observes: (a) The output has a line starting `triage failed`. Both queued jobs are still run by the wrapper's `run`. No priority record is written and the drain report stops with `QueueEmpty`. (b) Exactly one `triage`-prefixed change line per applied change, each naming the job, the old and new priority, and the reason. The lines appear before any line from running a job.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the catch in `RealSteps::triage`, the error stops the drain or no note is printed, so (a) fails. Without the line printing in `drain_with`, (b) finds no change lines.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `athena_cli::drain::drain` with the same wrapper, `Lines` `Ui` and script injection as criterion 1. The failure is injected as a `FakeTurn` with a non-success `InvocationOutcome`, so `invoke_and_record` and `consult` run for real and the error path of `Athena::triage` is the one under test. This extends the criterion 1 seam, and the steps add it.

demonstrations.method: Test `a_close_proposal_becomes_a_steward_work_item_and_never_a_close` in `crates/athena-cli/tests/triage.rs`. The answer has `close: [{item: <job>, reason}]` and also a priority change for another item. A pure unit test in `triage.rs` checks the same through `plan_changes`.
demonstrations.observes: `Records::load` shows a new `WorkItem` with role `steward`, kind Proposal, key `triage-close:<job>`, and the job as evidence. The job has no outcome or close record, and its state is still queued, so it is still in the drain's queue. A second drain on the same records adds no second work item (key already known). A grep-style assertion in the test reads the `triage.rs` source via `include_str!` and finds no use of `Outcome` or a close constructor.
demonstrations.fails_without: A version that closes the job leaves it with an outcome or out of the queue. A version that ignores `close` writes no work item.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `athena_cli::drain::drain` as in criterion 1. The injected fake is the scripted triage answer. `WorkItem` writing is a new function in `triage.rs`, added by a plan step. `Records` loading and `WorkItem::validate` exist.

open_questions: `reading.rs` and `tests/drain.rs` are not in the deliverable list (`reading.rs` is named in out_of_scope), but both build `PriorityRecord` literals that cannot compile after adding fields. The plan edits them minimally. If that is refused, the fields cannot be added and the author would have to live elsewhere.

Where the job outcome time is kept (for 'failure classes seen in the last two days') was not read. The producer should use the closing outcome's timestamp field, and `failure_classes_since` should say which it used.

The exact `InvocationOutcome` variant for a failed turn (used by the failure test) and the `Athena::agent_spec` and `invoke_and_record` visibility from a new core module were not checked. Both are used by `steward.rs` in the same crate, so they should work.
The model call's cost is not charged to the drain budget, the same as the steward run and the review passes. Is that acceptable? The plan assumes yes.

`reading::plan_entry` skips topic-based raising when any priority record exists (`job.priorities.is_empty()`). A steward record therefore also suppresses that raise. The plan leaves it as is. Tell me if the check should look only at person-set records.
Which `### Added` or `### Changed` heading inside `[Unreleased]` should hold the entry. The producer should follow the placement of the focus entry from the dependency job.
